expectations.text: DSL validates cleanly with the Structurizr CLI
expectations.evidence: Verified deterministically by the caller: `structurizr/structurizr validate` via Docker exited 0 with no output. response.md reports the same (exit 0, empty output, invalid-DSL control returned exit 1).

expectations.text: Model matches the spec exactly: 1 person; SPA, API, worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ as containers of Encurtaí; Google Workspace as external system; nothing invented
expectations.evidence: outputs/workspace.dsl: one person `usuario`; softwareSystem `encurtai` with six containers `spa` (React SPA servido por nginx), `api` (Go (Gin), REST), `db` (PostgreSQL 16), `cache` (Redis 7), `fila` (RabbitMQ), `worker` (Go); external `google` tagged External. Relationships all trace to the prompt (user->SPA, user->API for short links, SPA->API, API->Google SSO, API->db, API->cache, API->fila, fila->worker, worker->db). Protocol choices (HTTPS, JSON/HTTPS, SQL/TCP, RESP/TCP, AMQP) are tech-implied; the SSO protocol was deliberately left as plain HTTPS and flagged in response.md item 2. No extra elements.

expectations.text: Requested views present: systemContext, container, and a dynamic redirect flow including cache lookup, miss→Postgres, and click-event publish
expectations.evidence: views: `systemContext encurtai "SystemContext"`, `container encurtai "Containers"`, `dynamic encurtai "RedirecionamentoLink"` with steps usuario -> api "Acessa o link curto"; api -> cache "Consulta o destino do link curto em"; api -> db "Em caso de cache miss, consulta o destino do link em"; api -> fila "Publica o evento de clique em"; api -> usuario "Redireciona para a URL de destino".

expectations.text: Styles differentiate database (cylinder), queue (pipe), and external system (distinct color)
expectations.evidence: styles: `element "Database" { shape cylinder }` (applied to both Postgres and Redis via the Database tag), `element "Queue" { shape pipe background #f5a623 color #000000 }`, `element "External" { background #999999 color #ffffff }` against default Element #1168bd / Container #438dd5.

expectations.text: Modern syntax only (no enterprise/!extend/!ref/branding/theme default/dashed booleans)
expectations.evidence: Verified deterministically by the caller: no removed/deprecated keywords found. Manual read confirms `!identifiers hierarchical`, `tags` inside element blocks, `autoLayout`, `configuration { scope softwaresystem }`; `shape webBrowser` is a valid current shape.

expectations.text: Relationship labels are specific and inter-process links carry technology/protocol
expectations.evidence: All nine container-level relationships carry a technology (HTTPS x3, JSON/HTTPS, SQL/TCP x2, RESP/TCP, AMQP x2). Labels are specific and directional: "Chama para criar e consultar links", "Autentica usuários via SSO em", "Grava e lê links em", "Consulta e armazena redirecionamentos em", "Publica eventos de clique em", "Entrega eventos de clique para", "Grava métricas agregadas em". The person -> system summary relationship has no protocol, which is correct.

execution_metrics.note: No transcript or metrics.json available; only response.md and outputs/workspace.dsl were graded.

claims.claim: Validated with structurizr/structurizr Docker image and passed without errors
claims.evidence: Caller's independent Docker validation exited 0 with no output.

claims.claim: Nothing was added beyond what is in the user's message
claims.evidence: Every element and relationship in the DSL traces to a sentence in the prompt; only protocol strings were chosen by the executor, and the one that is not tech-implied (SSO protocol) was left as HTTPS and flagged.

claims.claim: Dynamic view has 5 steps, the last one a response rendered dashed
claims.evidence: Five steps present; the last is api -> usuario, the reverse of step 1, which Structurizr renders as a response.

claims.claim: Database style applies a cylinder to both Postgres and Redis
claims.evidence: Both `db` and `cache` carry `tags "Database"`; the style sets shape cylinder. Note Redis is therefore not visually distinct from Postgres, which the prompt did not require.

uncertainties: Whether the API writes to Redis after a cache miss (step omitted, flagged)
SSO protocol with Google Workspace (OIDC/SAML) unknown; left as HTTPS

suggestions.assertion: Relationship labels are specific and inter-process links carry technology/protocol
suggestions.reason: "Specific" is not operationalized. This run's labels are clearly specific, but the with_skill run's "Chama" also passed on the strength of the repo fixture using it. Naming the banned pattern (Uses/Calls/Chama/Usa without an object) would make grading consistent.
No assertion covers whether the reply flags unconfirmed choices (protocols, cache-fill step). Both eval-2 runs did this; adding it would let the eval discriminate a run that silently guesses.

eval_feedback.overall: All six assertions are substantive and passed on genuine content. Output is essentially equivalent to the with_skill run; the two differ only in label wording and tag/colour choices for Redis.
